\section*{Question 5}

Consider the differential equation \(\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{3-x}{y}\).
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Let \(y=f(x)\) be the particular solution to the given differential equation for \(1<x<5\) such that the line \(y=-2\) is tangent to the graph of \(f\). Find the \(x\)-coordinate of the point of tangency, and determine whether \(f\) has a local maximum, local minimum, or neither at this point. Justify your answer.
\item[(b)] Let \(y=g(x)\) be the particular solution to the given differential equation for \(-2<x<8\), with the initial condition \(g(6)=-4\). Find \(y=g(x)\).
\item[(a)] \(\frac{d y}{d x}=0\) when \(x=3\)
\[
\left.\frac{d^{2} y}{d x^{2}}\right|_{(3,-2)}=\left.\frac{-y-y^{\prime}(3-x)}{y^{2}}\right|_{(3,-2)}=\frac{1}{2},
\]
so \(f\) has a local minimum at this point. or
Because \(f\) is continuous for \(1<x<5\), there is an interval containing \(x=3\) on which \(y<0\). On this interval, \(\frac{d y}{d x}\) is negative to the left of \(x=3\) and \(\frac{d y}{d x}\) is positive to the right of \(x=3\). Therefore \(f\) has a local minimum at \(x=3\).
\item[(b)] \(y d y=(3-x) d x\)
\[
\begin{aligned}
& \frac{1}{2} y^{2}=3 x-\frac{1}{2} x^{2}+C \\
& 8=18-18+C ; C=8 \\
& y^{2}=6 x-x^{2}+16 \\
& y=-\sqrt{6 x-x^{2}+16}
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{itemize}
\(3\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: x=3 \\ 1: \text { local minimum } \\ 1: \text { justification }\end{array}\right.\)
\(6\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { separates variables } \\ 1: \text { antiderivative of } d y \text { term } \\ 1: \text { antiderivative of } d x \text { term } \\ 1: \text { constant of integration } \\ 1: \text { uses initial condition } g(6)=-4 \\ 1: \text { solves for } y\end{array}\right.\)
